newsitem.title: USA: NRC sees Salem 2 nuke restart approval by end-July.
newsitem.headline: NRC sees Salem 2 nuke restart approval by end-July.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Thursday it expected to grant approval to restart one of two idled units at the Salem nuclear power station in southern New Jersey by the end of July.
Asked when NRC's regional administrator would give clearance for Salem 2 to return to operation, NRC spokesman Neil Sheehan said, "It's safe to say by the end of month."
He declined to provide a specific date.
The NRC administrator is still studying a safety readiness review conducted by a 14-person NRC inspection team in early June, Sheehan said.
Salem 2 and the adjoining unit 1, each rated at 1,106 megawatts, have been shut since mid-1995 after NRC raised concerns over the units' safety.

On June 27, NRC's staff recommended to the regional chief to give the operator Public Service Electric & Gas Co (PSE&G) the go-ahead to restart Salem 2 after two years of addressing NRC's concerns over its operations, personnel, management and maintenance.
PSE&G, on the same day, submitted a letter to the regional administrator affirming that Salem 2 is ready to operate.
The readiness letter is the last regulatory requirement PSE&G must perform before the regional chief can authorize a restart for Salem 2.
In the NRC letter, PSE&G said Salem 2 is ready for restart and could enter into startup mode on or about Saturday.
PSE&G earlier said it aimed to restore Salem 1 to service in autumn.
In addition to PSE&G, owners of Salem are PECO Energy Co, Delmarva Power & Light Co and Atlantic Energy Co.
